newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products end mixed, gasoline supply tight.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products end mixed, gasoline supply tight.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products ended mixed on Friday as gasoline supplies held tight and gas oil retraced some of its recent gains, traders said.
Gasoline held steady on the back of solid demand from the eastern Mediterranean and a dearth of supplies that is expected to last through the first 10 days of Feb, traders said.
"The arb is still open to the States, freight rates are still expensive and eastern Mediterranean demand is not being met from the Med," said one trader in France.
Lebanon and Turkey remained short gasoline and the only extra supply in the Med, in Greece, is too expensive, he said.
Naphtha held steady as traders waited to see where four large cargoes would end up, either to NWE or trans-Atlantic.
Gas oil prices retraced much of Thursday's $7 gains as IPE gas oil futures eased and demand stayed thin.
Weaker NWE markets compounded the slack demand, good supply situation by cutting off another outlet for surplus Med product.
"Expensive freight cost have been prohibitive for arbitrage anywhere but weaker prices in the North will not help either," a trader said.
Quotes-related premiums for Russian gas oil cargoes remained pressured by ample supplies.
But premiums for FOD and diesel cargoes were steady. A refiner wanted EN90 product into Lavera.
Heavy fuel was steady as weakness from barges in Rotterdam was offset by demand for bunker fuel into Spain and West Afica.
High sulphur bunker fuel was well bid at $93.50 fob but sellers asked $95.00 for loading 5-10 february.

Low sulphur was also flat amid poor Italian demand. Enel, Italy's state power company, is covered for February and saw few offers even for March delivery. Prices were pegged around $116.00 cif Italy amid trade abetween $106.00 and $107.00 for February low sulphur cargo swaps in northwest Europe.
